items.question: What is the best time to visit Mount Bromo?
items.answer: May through September (dry season) is the best time for Mount Bromo. Clear skies at dawn produce the iconic sea-of-clouds sunrise over the Tengger Caldera. July and August are the peak months but attract the largest crowds. April and October offer nearly identical conditions with fewer visitors and lower accommodation rates.

items.question: When can you see the Ijen blue fire?
items.answer: Ijen blue fire is visible year-round during JVTO night hikes, but May to October offers the clearest sightlines — lower humidity, less cloud cover inside the crater, and drier trail conditions on the descent to the sulfur lake. Blue flames from burning sulfur gases appear most vivid between midnight and 03:00 AM regardless of month. JVTO night hikes depart at around 00:00–01:00 AM to reach the crater by the peak blue-fire window.

items.question: Is Tumpak Sewu waterfall better in wet season or dry season?
items.answer: Tumpak Sewu is most impressive in the wet season (January–April) when waterfall volume peaks after sustained rainfall. The curtain of 120+ individual falls is at its widest and most powerful during this period. However, the descent trail through Glidih Canyon becomes slippery and rope-assisted sections require care. The dry season (May–October) offers safer, drier footing with still-impressive flow. JVTO guides assess trail conditions on arrival before starting the descent.

items.question: What months make up the rainy season in East Java?
items.answer: East Java's rainy season typically runs from November through March, with December and January being the wettest months. Rain usually falls as heavy afternoon and evening showers rather than continuous drizzle, so morning tours to Bromo and Ijen are still viable. Tours are not automatically cancelled in the rainy season — JVTO monitors BMKG and PVMBG forecasts before each departure and decides based on real conditions.

items.question: What is the peak tourist season in East Java?
items.answer: Peak season is July and August, coinciding with European summer school holidays and Indonesian National Day (17 August). Bromo sunrise viewpoints at Penanjakan are significantly busier, and accommodation in the Tengger Caldera area books out quickly. JVTO private tours operate normally during peak season, but we recommend booking at least 3–4 weeks ahead for July–August departures.

items.question: What is the coldest month at Ijen Crater?
items.answer: July and August are the coldest months at Ijen Crater. Pre-dawn temperatures at the crater rim (2,386 m) can drop to 5–8°C, and the descent to the sulfur lake adds wind-chill exposure. JVTO provides a gas mask for all guests as standard. Guests should bring a warm jacket, gloves, and a wind layer — especially for July–August night hikes.

items.question: Is December a good time to visit Bromo?
items.answer: December marks the start of the rainy season and cloud cover at dawn is more frequent than in dry season. Sunrise conditions are less predictable — roughly 40–50% of departures in December–January encounter partial or full cloud cover at the Penanjakan viewpoint. JVTO monitors BMKG the evening before every tour and advises guests when forecasts look poor. A clear December sunrise is still possible; it is simply less guaranteed than May–September.

items.question: What is the best single month to visit all three destinations?
items.answer: May or September offer the best combination: dry-season conditions for Bromo and Ijen, decent Tumpak Sewu flow (not peak, but still strong), and significantly fewer crowds than July–August. May and September also tend to have lower accommodation rates. If Tumpak Sewu waterfall volume is your priority over everything else, March or April (late wet season) is the better choice — but expect wet trail conditions and pack accordingly.
